title: Most people never notice this.
paragraphs: Most people never notice this.
The first man in Scripture to take more than one wife was not introduced as wise, blessed, righteous, or favored by God.
He was introduced as violent.
That is not an accident.

The first polygamist in the Bible was Lamech, a descendant of Cain — the same bloodline that flowed from the first murderer in human history. And the moment Scripture introduces polygamy into the human story, it places it inside a family line already corrupted by rebellion, pride, vengeance, and bloodshed.
God saw it.
And He recorded it exactly as it happened.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The Bible often describes things without approving them.

Many people assume that because certain men in the Old Testament practiced polygamy, God must have endorsed it. But Scripture repeatedly shows the destruction, jealousy, division, and spiritual decay that followed it.
The very first appearance of polygamy sets the tone.

Violence.
Pride.
Self-exaltation.
Defiance against God’s design.
You knew there was something deeper there.
God’s Original Design Was One Man and One Woman
Before sin entered the world, God established marriage in Eden.
The Hebrew text of Genesis 2:24 says:
“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.”
In Hebrew:

וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד
ve-davaq be-ishto ve-hayu le-vasar echad
Key phrases matter here.
“His wife” — Singular
The Hebrew word:

אִשְׁתּוֹ (ishto)
“his wife”
Singular.
Not wives.
From the beginning, God’s covenant pattern was covenantal unity between one man and one woman becoming “one flesh.”
Jesus Himself later reaffirmed this in the Greek text of Matthew 19:4–6.
“Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female…”
Greek:

ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς
arsen kai thēly epoiēsen autous
“male and female He made them”
Then Christ quotes Genesis directly and concludes:
“What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.”
Jesus did not point to polygamy as the model.
He pointed back to Eden.
Back before sin multiplied corruption.
Back before human rebellion distorted covenant.
Cain’s Line: Civilization Without God
Genesis 4 presents two family lines developing in parallel.

Cain’s descendants advanced culturally:
cities,
music,
metalworking,
technology.
But spiritually, the line became increasingly corrupted.
Then suddenly Genesis 4:19 says:
“And Lamech took unto him two wives…”
Hebrew:

וַיִּקַּח־לוֹ לֶמֶךְ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
vayyiqqach-lo Lemech shtei nashim
Literally:
“Lamech took for himself two women/wives.”
The wording matters.
“Taken for himself.”
Self-directed desire.
Not divine instruction.
Not covenant blessing.
Not God speaking.
Lamech becomes the first human in biblical history to violate the one-man-one-woman pattern established in Eden.
And immediately after introducing his polygamy, Scripture records a chilling song of violence.
That sequence is intentional.
Lamech’s Song of Violence
Genesis 4:23–24 is one of the darkest speeches in early human history.
Lamech says to his wives:

“Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech:
for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.”
Hebrew:

כִּי אִישׁ הָרַגְתִּי לְפִצְעִי
ki ish haragti le-fitz‘i
“For I killed a man for wounding me”
And then:
“If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.”
Hebrew:

שִׁבְעִים וְשִׁבְעָה
shiv‘im ve-shiv‘ah
“seventy-sevenfold”
This is not repentance.
This is boastful escalation.
Cain murdered and feared judgment.
Lamech murders and celebrates himself.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this moment reveals something terrifying about unchecked sin: it never stays still.

Violence grows.
Pride grows.
Sexual rebellion grows.
Human self-worship grows.
Sin always evolves toward greater corruption unless God intervenes.
The Connection Between Violence and Sexual Corruption
The placement of this passage matters deeply.
The Bible could have introduced polygamy anywhere.
But God chose to introduce it in the context of a violent, arrogant man descended from Cain.
That literary structure is theological.
Scripture is showing the unraveling of creation order.
One rebellion leads to another.
When humans reject God’s authority in one area, corruption spreads into others.
Paul later explains this spiritual principle in Romans 1.

People suppress truth,
exchange God’s design,
then become consumed by disordered desires and violence.
Sin never remains isolated.
You see this pattern throughout the Old Testament.

Nearly every major polygamous household becomes marked by:
jealousy,
division,
competition,
sexual sin,
family destruction,
or bloodshed.

Abraham and Hagar.
Jacob with Leah and Rachel.
David’s fractured household.
Solomon’s downfall.
The pattern repeats again and again.
Not because God approved of it.
But because Scripture tells the truth about fallen humanity.
God saw it.
What About the Patriarchs?
Many skeptics ask:
“If polygamy was wrong, why did God allow it?”
Because God often permits what He does not endorse.

The same Scriptures that record polygamy also record:
divorce,
slavery,
idolatry,
human sacrifice,
murder,
and rebellion.
Description is not approval.
Jesus explained this principle regarding divorce in Matthew 19:8:
“Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.”
From the beginning.
Christ keeps bringing humanity back to God’s original design.

Not cultural normalization.
Not fallen tradition.
Not human appetite.
Truth.
The Hebrew Structure Reveals a Warning
There is another detail many readers miss.

Genesis 4 contrasts two voices:
Cain’s corrupted lineage
and Seth’s godly lineage in Genesis 5.
Lamech from Cain’s line boasts in violence.
But later another Lamech — from Seth’s line — speaks hope over Noah.
Genesis 5:29:
“This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands…”
Hebrew:

זֶה יְנַחֲמֵנוּ
zeh yenachamenu
“This one will comfort us”
One Lamech glorifies vengeance.
The other longs for redemption.
The contrast is intentional.

Two spiritual paths.
Two legacies.
Two kingdoms.

One built on pride and self-rule.
The other waiting for God’s mercy.
Christ Reverses the Curse of Violent Men
The Gospel does not merely condemn sinners.
It rescues them.
Lamech bragged about seventy-sevenfold vengeance.
But Jesus later transformed that number entirely.
In Matthew 18:22, when Peter asked how many times forgiveness should be offered, Jesus answered:
“Until seventy times seven.”
Greek:

ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά
heōs hebdomēkontakis hepta
Lamech used “seventy-seven” for revenge.
Jesus used it for mercy.
That is not coincidence.
That is redemption overturning the spirit of Cain.

The kingdom of darkness multiplies vengeance.
The kingdom of Christ multiplies forgiveness.
Only Jesus can reverse what sin has corrupted.
Only Christ can transform violent hearts into redeemed hearts.
Only the cross can reconcile what rebellion destroyed.
Because at the center of human corruption is not merely bad behavior.
It is sin.
And sin separates humanity from God.
That is why Jesus came.

Not simply to improve morality.
Not merely to repair culture.
But to save sinners through His blood.
The Greek of John 3:16 declares:

Οὕτως γὰρ ἠγάπησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν κόσμον
Houtōs gar ēgapēsen ho Theos ton kosmon
“For God so loved the world…”
Christ entered the violence of humanity and absorbed judgment at the cross.
The innocent One died for the guilty.
The sinless One carried sinners.
The risen Christ now calls every person to repentance and faith.

Not self-justification.
Not religious performance.
Repentance.
Faith.
Surrender.
Because the same sinful nature that existed in Cain and Lamech still exists in humanity now.

Pride.
Lust.
Violence.
Self-rule.
You knew.
God saw it.
And yet Christ still offers mercy.
If this exposed something inside you, don’t ignore it. Write “Jesus is Lord” if you know only Christ can change the human heart.
